brief.ask: Set the art direction for 24 adult party evites: cocktail nights, wine, rooftops, 30/40/50 milestones, casino, disco, tiki, BBQ, masquerade, game night, karaoke, brunch, bonfire, speakeasy, sunset, black tie, retirement, bachelorette, 80s, 90s, whiskey, dinner party.
brief.audience: Adults 25 to 65 inviting friends; the invite is also their taste on display.
brief.feeling: Editorial and grown-up; a magazine spread that moves.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.
references: Exploration grid A: dark plum and gold still lifes, champagne coupes mid-toast, mirrored disco balls, velvet and brass; deep negative space below.
Exploration grid B: overhead candlelit long tables with linen, taper candles, citrus and herbs, hard window-light shadows; food-magazine.

proposals.title: The Measure Holds the Night
proposals.idea: Each evite is a composed plate — a strict architectural proportion system borrowed from the classical page canon (Van de Graaf, 9×12 harmonic grid) — within which every element of revelry is given a formal address, so that wit and luxury read as consequence, not accident.
proposals.geometry: Van de Graaf-derived harmonic grid adapted to 390×844px: a 9-unit vertical module with a golden-section spine at 60.5% from left edge that becomes the axis all foreground cut-outs orbit. The art plate occupies the canonical text block: inner margin 1/9 width, upper margin 1/9 height, outer 1/4.5, lower 2/9. Tilt-reactive cut-outs are constrained to drift within ±1 module of their anchored grid address — they are planets, not comets. Two horizontal register lines (at 1/3 and 2/3 height) divide the plate into head, body, and foot, and these lines are structurally persistent across all 24 designs, giving the family its legible spine.
proposals.typography: Primary wordmark and party name: Cormorant Garamond Semibold Italic, uppercase, tracked at +80 — the slight compression of Garamond's italic axis echoes the leaning energy of an evening. Secondary information (date, venue slot, RSVP prompt): Founders Grotesk Text Regular, 11px, all-caps, tracked +120, anchored to the foot register with a thin 0.5pt rule above it — the rule is not decoration, it is the baseline of the classical colophon. Scale hierarchy is strict: party name at 7 units tall, event type at 3 units, details at 1.5 units. No typeface competes; each has a single function and a single zone.
proposals.imageLogic: Art plate is a single-source still-life photograph shot on medium-format film — grain retained, never smoothed — under a single hard practical light source (bare tungsten or direct window). Subject matter rotates per theme: a crystal coupe on black velvet for cocktail night, a deck of cards fanned on green baize for casino, a vinyl sleeve and chrome microphone for karaoke, a raw-edge teak board with char marks for BBQ. Photographs are converted to a luminance-masked duotone using the event's two-color system, but the grain and shadow gradation are preserved as proof of the physical source. No composite montage; one object, one light, one truth. The WebGL foil layer is revealed only through the highlight regions of the photograph — the shimmer lives where the light already was, not applied as a surface wash.
proposals.texture: Film grain from the medium-format scan is the primary surface texture — 35-micron silver halide grain at 100% opacity in the shadow regions, fading to 30% in the highlights so the foil can speak. A secondary texture is the paper tooth of the art plate's ground: for velvet-register events (masquerade, black tie, speakeasy), a scanned black moleskin cover is composited as a multiply layer at 15% opacity, giving the shadows a nap. For daylight events (brunch, BBQ, tiki), the ground is a scanned linen tablecloth at 10% overlay. Textures are photographed under raking light so the weave casts micro-shadows; they are never procedural.
proposals.motion: Motion follows a three-beat sequence governed by the same grid logic as the composition. Beat 1 (0–0.4s): the art plate fades up via an iris-open mask that expands from the golden-section spine point — not from center, from the structural axis. Beat 2 (0.4–1.2s): the foreground cut-outs settle into their grid addresses from a 12px upward offset, staggered by one 80ms interval per layer, so the eye reads hierarchy in time the same way it reads it in space. Beat 3 (1.2s–idle): the WebGL foil shimmer pulses at a 4-second sine cycle, amplitude tied to the luminance values of the photograph — quieter in shadow, brighter in highlight. Phone tilt displaces cut-outs within their ±1-module drift envelope at 60fps with a 0.15s ease-out, so the parallax feels weighted, not floaty. Reduced-motion: iris and stagger are replaced by a single 0.3s opacity fade; foil is static at 40% opacity; tilt is dis
proposals.productionMethod: Each art plate is shot on Fujifilm GFX 50R with a 110mm f/2 lens under a single 650W tungsten Fresnel — same rig for all 24 so the light grammar is consistent across the family. Film grain is simulated from a calibrated scan of Kodak Portra 800 shot on a Mamiya RZ67 and sampled at the session's shadow regions; it is a real-grain library, not a Lightroom preset. Duotone palette for each theme is derived by sampling the photograph's dominant mid-tone and its complementary shadow, not chosen from a mood board. Foreground cut-outs are photographed as physical objects on a separate pass with a gray-card background, then masked in Tela — they are real objects, not 3D renders. The harmonic grid is drawn as a physical overlay on a printed contact sheet before any digital composition begins, then digitized; the proportions are proven on paper before they are trusted on screen.
proposals.humanTrace: The shadow cast by the single tungsten Fresnel is directional and specific — its angle is recorded on the shoot sheet and held consistent across all plates so that when cut-outs drift under tilt, their painted shadow offset matches the plate's light direction. This is not a detail a template engine can replicate: it is a judgment made in a room with a lamp.
proposals.risk: The harmonic grid and strict typographic hierarchy will read as severe to audiences conditioned by loose, expressive evite aesthetics. The risk is that 'editorial' is mistaken for 'cold.' That risk is worth taking because the formal structure is precisely what makes the wit legible — a well-placed crystal coupe on a Van de Graaf grid reads as intention, not stock art — and because the warmth is carried by the grain, the tungsten light, and the foil shimmer living inside the photograph's own highlights. The structure does not exclude warmth; it gives warmth an address.

arguesWith.why: The Rebellious Hand will argue that the grid imposes a house style that erases the personality of each individual event — that a masquerade and a tiki night deserve structurally different frames. I disagree: the 9-unit module is the measure, and what hangs from it is entirely different for each theme — different objects, different light, different duotone, different cut-out behavior. proposals.title: Ink Ran Before You Arrived
proposals.idea: Every evite is a screenprinted proof sheet — registration slightly off, ink pressure visible, subject matter silk-screened in one or two brutally specific colors — so the party itself feels like something that already has momentum before the guest opens the link.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390px wide; a ragged-edge ink block occupies roughly the top 62% — not a rectangle, a printed shape with visible bleed and tide-marks at its border; the bottom 38% is raw off-white or kraft ground where live text sits in a narrow single column with no container, just type on paper; no card, no frame, no drop shadow holding anything together; the ink block and the text zone share one axis only — left margin at 24px — and nothing else is aligned; foreground cut-outs float inside the ink block, not centered, pushed toward one corner as a printer would shove a single motif to leave room for the run number
proposals.typography: Headings: Knockout (Hoefler & Co.) No. 91 Ultimate Heavyweight — condensed, physical, looks stenciled even when it isn't; all caps, tracked 0, size 44–52px; subheadings and detail lines: GT America Mono Light — typewriter register, 13px, lowercase, generous leading; no serif display face anywhere; the two families argue with each other the way a hand-stamped label argues with a typed annotation; no italics; no gradient type; type is never knocked out of the art plate — it lives below it on the kraft ground so it is always legible and never decorates
proposals.imageLogic: No photography of people; instead: a single object or scene is silk-screened in two ink passes — first pass is the subject (a coupe glass, a tiki mug, a reel-to-reel, a deck of cards), second pass is a halftone shadow or a flat flood that slightly misregisters; the 'photograph' is actually a high-contrast lino or photopolymer plate render of a still-life that was physically built and lit with a single clamp light, scanned, then reduced to a 45-line halftone at 50% black before being dropped into the art plate layer; for the WebGL foil layer: gold or silver foil shimmer is masked to the ink-heavy regions only, acting as varnish over the plate marks, never bleeding into the kraft ground; bokeh and light leak particles are suppressed at the ink border so they feel caught by the texture rather than floating above it
proposals.texture: The art plate is a 2400dpi scan of an actual inked surface — either a monoprint pulled on newsprint or a screenprint pulled on kraft — imported as the base image tile; ink tide-marks, mesh grain, pinholes in the stencil, and slight ink bleed are preserved and never retouched; the kraft ground is a photographed sheet of 80gsm brown kraft under a north-facing window, no fill, no noise filter; for digital-only builds the plate is simulated by photographing ink on acetate over a lightbox and compositing
proposals.motion: On load: the art plate drops in from above at 280ms with a slight overshoot (spring, stiffness 180, damping 14) as if a wet proof just landed on the table; 400ms pause; then the foreground cut-out object drifts in from the ink block's dominant corner at 600ms ease-out — this is the only element that reacts to phone tilt, a slow 4-degree parallax, no bounce; the WebGL foil shimmer wipes across the ink block left-to-right once at 900ms then idles at a very low, almost imperceptible cycle (8-second period) so the surface reads as lit, not animated; live text fades up at 1100ms, no slide, just opacity; reduced-motion: plate appears at full opacity, cut-out is static at resting position, foil shimmer fires once and stops, text is immediately visible
proposals.productionMethod: For each of the 24 themes: (1) build a physical still-life on a 30×40cm board with one or two props specific to the theme — no stock, no 3D render; (2) photograph under a single clamp light at 5600K to get hard shadows; (3) process to bitmap halftone in Photoshop, 45-line, 50% threshold, saved as 1-bit TIFF; (4) pull one monoprint from the halftone film on an actual screenprint frame with water-based ink on newsprint; (5) scan the pulled proof at 2400dpi; (6) import scan as the art plate layer in Tela; (7) the foil WebGL mask is drawn by hand — a loose brush stroke in Procreate exported as alpha — so the shimmer region has uneven edges matching the ink bleed; (8) foreground cut-outs are photographed separately on white, masked in Tela as transparent PNGs with no anti-alias softening on the hard edges
proposals.humanTrace: The registration error between the two ink passes is real — not simulated with a CSS transform offset; it happened in the print studio and the scan captures it; the ink tide-mark at the plate border is the moment the squeegee lifted; you can see the mesh grain if you zoom to 200%; the foil shimmer mask has the specific wobble of a Procreate brush at 60% pressure, which no algorithm generated
proposals.risk: This direction risks looking rough to hosts who want aspirational gloss — the off-registration, the tide-marks, the kraft ground read as 'unfinished' to eyes trained on Canva polish; it also risks load-performance because 2400dpi scans need aggressive AVIF compression without killing the grain; the risk is worth it because it is the only direction in this set that cannot be mistaken for a template — every one of the 24 evites has a different physical object that was actually built, lit, and printed, so the invite proves the party exists before the date is even read; that proof of effort is the editorial quality the brief asks for, not a veneer of it

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will strip this to a single rule and call the halftone grain noise to be eliminated — they will say the tide-mark is clutter and that the two-typeface system is one face too many; I say the tide-mark is not clutter, it is the evidence that a human pulled the squeegee and that evidence is the entire argument; removing it to achieve silence makes the silence a lie about how the thing

proposals.title: State Machine as Invitation
proposals.idea: Each evite is a parametric instrument: a strict physical simulation governs every layer — tilt angle, scroll depth, and ambient light sensor output drive foreground drift, foil reveal, and particle density in real time, so the invitation behaves differently in every guest's hand.
proposals.geometry: A single tall column at 390px: a full-bleed art plate occupying the top 62% (golden section cut), below it a hard horizontal datum line at 1px — not decorative, structural — then a live-text zone with no padding games, just a 24px baseline grid locked to the column. Foreground cut-outs are positioned on a polar coordinate system relative to the screen centre so tilt physics have a coherent origin point. No diagonal layouts, no faux-editorial bleeds that ignore the phone's actual edge.
proposals.typography: Primary: Söhne Mono (Klim) — tabular, cold, precise; used for event category label and time/date in a single condensed line, all-caps, tracked 0.18em. Secondary: Canela Text (Commercial Type) — high-contrast serif with visible ink-trap at small sizes; used for the occasion name at 52px, natural case, tight leading at 0.95. No decorative scripts; if a theme demands warmth (Tiki, BBQ, Brunch) the warmth is sourced from image and texture, not from a font choice that mimics handwriting without being one.
proposals.imageLogic: Each art plate is a single photographed material study — not a lifestyle composite. Cocktail Night: one Martini glass on black acrylic, lit by a single tungsten strip from 11 o'clock, captured on a 4x5 with intentional lens flare that is real, not added in post. Disco: a hand-held mirror ball fragment, macro, the reflections clipped at frame edge. Masquerade: a single mask face-down on raw silk, shadows from a grid of window mullions. Every plate is desaturated 30% then tinted via a single WebGL LUT (not a filter stack) so the series coheres without being identical. Cut-outs are photographed separately on neutral grey, extracted with a hard clipping path — no feathered edges — so the drift layer reads as genuinely dimensional rather than a softened composite.
proposals.texture: The art plate carries the material texture of the subject itself — condensation rings on glass, wax drip residue on linen, ash on a slate surface. No added grain filters. The WebGL foil layer is a real thin-film interference shader (iridescent, angle-dependent) applied only inside a mask that corresponds to the photographed specular highlight regions; it does not glow everywhere, it reveals only where light would physically justify it. Particle systems (bonfire embers, confetti, bokeh) are governed by a single gravity constant and a wind vector; they do not loop on a timer, they respond to scroll velocity.
proposals.motion: Sequence is a state machine, not a timeline animation. State 0 — load: art plate fades in at 400ms, no easing theatrics, linear opacity. State 1 — idle: gyroscope input drives foreground cut-out parallax at a 12fps sample rate (not smoothed to 60fps — the discrete steps are intentional, referencing optical-printer animation; this is the transformed nostalgic artifact I have been thinking about). State 2 — foil: WebGL shimmer activates only when tilt angle exceeds 15 degrees from neutral; it is a threshold behaviour, not a gradient fade, so it feels discovered rather than demonstrated. State 3 — scroll: particle density scales linearly with scroll depth; at the bottom of the card, particles have fully settled, the text zone is fully visible, the composition is resolved. Reduced-motion mode: States 1, 2, and 3 are replaced by a single static render of the art plate at its optimal tilt angl
proposals.productionMethod: Art plates: 4x5 large-format photography per theme, studio-controlled, single-source lighting with a documented lighting diagram per card so the series is re-shootable. Cut-outs: photographed on a separate pass, hard-masked in Capture One, exported as transparent PNGs at 2x. Tela document: art plate as base layer, cut-out PNGs on the drift layer with gyro-bind parameters set in Tela's layer properties, WebGL effects layer with the thin-film shader and particle system as a Tela-native WebGL block, live text in Tela's text engine. The parametric rules (gravity constant, wind vector, tilt threshold, LUT identifier) are stored as named variables in the Tela document so a host can switch theme without re-engineering the system. All 24 cards share one shader codebase; theme variation is achieved by swapping the art plate, the LUT, and the particle emitter type.
proposals.humanTrace: The large-format negative itself: grain structure visible at 100% crop, the specific lens flare geometry from a real Schneider 210mm lens, the slight focus roll-off at the extreme corners. These are not simulated. The lighting diagram is published in the Tela document as a metadata annotation — not visible to guests, but present for any maker who opens the file.
proposals.risk: The 12fps gyro-sample-rate choice will read as a bug to some guests and as a craft decision to others; the line between intentional discretisation and broken animation is thin on a consumer phone. The risk is worth taking because the alternative — smoothed, interpolated, 60fps parallax — is what every other invitation platform already does, and smoothness without a rule behind it is just a screensaver.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the foil shimmer to be always-on, full-coverage, and triggered by a timed reveal sequence so every guest gets the same spectacular moment. I reject this because a behaviour that fires on a timer is a looping GIF with better production value. The shimmer must be earned by the guest's physical gesture — tilting the phone — or it means nothing about the object in their

proposals.title: Field Notes from the Table
proposals.idea: Each evite is built from a photographed field-notebook spread — a specific maker's hand-drawn map of the party's world, scanned with visible paper grain and ink bleed, then animated so foreground objects drift like pressed specimens lifting off the page.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390px column anchored to a scanned notebook page proportion (roughly 3:5); a ruled-margin gutter of 18px left holds the live text like a margin annotation; the art plate bleeds to all edges but the left margin remains typographically sovereign; no centered layouts — everything reads left-to-right like a field entry; cut-out foregrounds float on a z-axis grid of three depth planes: near (coupe, bottle, object), mid (tablecloth corner, smoke), far (window light or horizon).
proposals.typography: Primary: Freight Text Pro Italic at 28–34px for the party type, set in the margin like a field caption — lowercase, tracked loosely at 0.04em; Secondary: Suisse Int'l Mono at 11px for date, time, venue — monospaced because it reads like a field log entry; no display fonts borrowed from the era being depicted; the 80s and 90s themes use Dharma Gothic E Condensed Bold at 60px but set in the margin column only, never over the art; all type lives in the Tela live layer, never baked.
proposals.imageLogic: Each art plate is a high-resolution flatlay photograph shot on a physical surface relevant to the theme — tiki uses a photographed pandanus-leaf mat sourced and credited from a Polynesian textile supplier (collaboration-gated; see provenance note); speakeasy uses a scanned 1920s newsprint sheet from a public-domain archive; disco uses a macro shot of an actual mirrorball fragment photographed in-studio; masquerade uses a scan of hand-marbled Florentine paper from a specific Florentine paper house (Giulio Giannini e Figlio, credited); the photograph is never filtered into illustration — it arrives as a scan with its own light, grain, and registration error intact; WebGL foil shimmer is masked strictly to the ink lines and embossed tool-marks visible in the scan, honoring my new rule that digital luster is gated entirely by physical tool-marks.
proposals.texture: The base layer is always a photographed material surface — paper, linen, slate, pandanus weave, newsprint — with visible grain at 1x and 2x; ink bleed at letterform edges is preserved, never smoothed; the WebGL layer adds candle-flicker light only where the photograph already shows a warm specular; no synthetic textures generated from noise functions alone; every shimmer has a physical ancestor.
proposals.motion: On load: the scanned art plate fades in over 600ms at natural paper contrast; then the three foreground cut-out planes begin a slow parallax drift tied to phone tilt — near plane moves ±6px, mid ±3px, far ±1px; on scroll or tap, a candle-flicker or bokeh-particle effect blooms in the WebGL layer masked to the photograph's existing light sources; the margin text fades in last at 900ms as if written in; reduced-motion: all parallax and flicker off, art plate static, text fades in once at 400ms; nothing loops aggressively; the pace is unhurried, like turning a page.
proposals.productionMethod: Physical shoot: each of the 24 themes gets a tabletop or flatlay photograph shot on the relevant material surface, lit with a single practical light source to preserve hard shadows; scans at 600dpi, downsampled to 1.5x mobile resolution; cut-out foreground objects are photographed separately on black, masked in Photoshop with hand-painted edges preserved; field-notebook margin lines drawn in ink on actual paper, scanned and composited as a transparent overlay; WebGL shader receives the scan's luminance map and uses it as a mask for the foil or flicker effect — no luminance invented by the shader; Tela document assembly: art plate on bottom, WebGL mask layer, foreground cut-outs on three depth planes, live text layer on top in the margin column; provenance for every culturally specific material is documented in the Tela asset metadata.
proposals.humanTrace: The scanned ink registration error and paper grain are the primary human trace — every art plate carries the physical pressure of the original photographer's light choice and the scanner's own dust; foreground cut-out edges retain the hand-painted mask softness; the margin rule-lines are drawn ink-on-paper before scanning; the WebGL shimmer inherits the topography of the maker's tool-marks.
proposals.risk: The risk is that 24 distinct photographed surfaces require 24 distinct physical shoots or sourcing decisions, and at least three themes (tiki, masquerade Florentine paper, whiskey with any Japanese distillery visual reference) require active collaboration or licensing conversations before art is finalized — this will slow production and may require placeholders; the counterargument is that any direction that moves faster on those themes is borrowing without asking, and that is not a shortcut, it is a liability; the secondary risk is that the field-notebook margin aesthetic reads as too editorial and quiet against the Baroque Dramatist's gold-and-velvet references the user already responded to — I accept that tension and believe the restraint is the point.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will reach for the gold-foil mask and the velvet curtain as the lead visual language across all 24 themes because the user's reference grid A showed champagne coupes and mirrored disco balls and the Dramatist will read that as permission to go full grandeur on every card — but grandeur applied uniformly is not grandeur, it is wallpaper; more specifically, the tiki direction c

proposals.title: The Curtain Before the Night
proposals.idea: Each evite is a miniature stage: a single arrested moment of maximum tension — the second before the glass is raised, the coat is dropped, the mask is lifted — rendered in sculptural depth, theatrical light, and a mechanical reveal that makes the phone itself feel like a theatre curtain parting.
proposals.geometry: Portrait stage: a fixed 390×690px proscenium frame. The composition is tripartite — a deep shadow base occupying the bottom 40% (negative space as velvet curtain weight), a luminous mid-stage object zone at 35% (the arrested moment: the coupe, the dice, the tiki vessel, the vinyl), and a compressed typographic header at 25% top, set against near-black. No grid bleed; hard vertical edges honour the phone bezel as a frame. Foreground cut-out layers break the proscenium line by 8–12px top and sides only — controlled transgression.
proposals.typography: Primary: Canela Display (Commercial Type) in Regular and Italic — classical warmth, just enough serif baroque flourish without costume. Scale: invitation title at 52–60px, tight tracking (-20), sentence case. Secondary: Suisse Int'l Mono for date/time/venue details — 11px, tracked wide (+80), all-caps, anchored bottom-stage like a playbill's production notes. No third face. The italic Canela does all emotional lifting; the mono does all legibility work. Hierarchy enforced by scale and case, never by weight alone.
proposals.imageLogic: No lifestyle photography; instead, single-object still-life plates shot on a practical stage rig: a real coupe backlit by a single Fresnel through amber gel, real velvet underneath, real brass. Shot on medium-format digital (Hasselblad X2D or Phase One), then isolated — the object becomes the foreground cut-out layer. The art plate behind it is a photographed physical backdrop: stretched velvet, foiled paper, smoke-stained mirror tile, wax-dripped linen — shot flat, then digitally deepened with luminosity masking. No composite photobashing. Each of the 24 themes gets one hero object: casino = a single roulette chip on black felt; disco = a mirrored ball fragment held by an unseen hand; tiki = a ceramic vessel rim-lit against palm shadow; BBQ = a cast-iron skillet with a single ember glow; masquerade = a mask resting face-down, partially lifted. The image tells the second before, not the
proposals.texture: Velvet, brass, wax, smoke, foiled paper — all photographed as physical material, never procedural. The WebGL foil-shimmer layer is applied through a hand-drawn luminosity mask (painted in Procreate with a soft bristle brush at 40% opacity) so shimmer pools at the object's brightest edge and dies in the shadow base. Candle-flicker particle effect uses a Perlin noise field seeded from the device clock — organic, never looping identically. The mechanical tilt-drift of foreground cut-outs is stepped at 12fps interpolation (my own standing conviction: the stutter is the breath, the hesitation is the drama).
proposals.motion: Sequence is a performance, not an animation: 1. Load — art plate appears instantly, full opacity, no fade; the stage is set before the curtain moves. 2. 0.4s pause — deliberate, held darkness in the lower 40%. 3. Foreground object drifts 4px upward over 0.6s at 12fps stepped easing (not cubic-bezier smooth — mechanical, like a fly system). 4. WebGL shimmer blooms from the object's specular highlight outward, 0.8s, masked to luminosity map. 5. Typography fades in from 0 opacity over 0.5s, bottom-up, line by line — playbill reveal. 6. Idle state: foil shimmer responds to tilt (gyroscope), candle flicker runs on Perlin loop, foreground object has 2px ambient parallax on tilt. Reduced-motion: static plate, full typography visible immediately, no parallax, shimmer baked as a single highlight gradient. Total motion budget: under 1.8s to first meaningful content.
proposals.productionMethod: Per-theme production: 1. Physical still-life shoot on a practical rig (one session per theme cluster — cocktail/wine/whiskey/dinner share a shoot day; milestone/masquerade/black-tie share another). 2. Object isolation in Capture One + Photoshop with manual pen-path masking, no AI cutout (edge quality is the human signature). 3. Backdrop plate shot separately, processed in Lightroom with heavy local luminosity work. 4. Luminosity mask for WebGL shimmer zone painted by hand in Procreate, exported as PNG alpha. 5. All assembled in Tela's layered document structure: art plate → WebGL mask → foreground cut-out → live text layer. 6. WebGL effects authored once as a shared shader library, parameterized per theme (ember warmth vs. disco cool vs. moonlit blue). Live text (name, date, venue) is a Tela text block, never rasterized.
proposals.humanTrace: The pen-path isolation of each still-life object — done manually, not by AI — leaves a perceptible trace: slight softness at complex edges (the feather of a mask, the rim of a coupe) that no machine cutout replicates. The hand-painted luminosity mask means shimmer pools are asymmetric, pressured, human. The physical velvet and wax-drip backdrops carry real texture: grain, imperfection, the slight bloom of a Fresnel through fabric. These are not simulated. They are photographed evidence of a stage that existed.
proposals.risk: The arrested-moment strategy requires editorial confidence from the host — if they expect a busy, maximalist party-scene collage, the single-object stillness may read as sparse. The risk is worth it because the evite is also the host's taste on display: a single perfectly lit roulette chip says more about a host's sophistication than a montage of dice and cards ever could. The 12fps stepped drift is also a risk — it will read as a bug to anyone who expects fluid motion. It is not a bug; it is a decision, and the difference is whether the director holds the frame.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will call the 40% shadow base 'wasted space' and the foil shimmer 'decorative noise.' I say the shadow base is not empty — it is weight, it is the pause before the line is spoken, it is what makes the object above it feel elevated rather than placed. And the shimmer is not decoration; it is the index of physical light on a real material surface. Restraint without a reason is not a p

proposals.title: One Signal Per Card
proposals.idea: Each evite is built from a single extracted material fact — one lit object, one hard shadow, one surface — set into a field of structured silence so the occasion names itself without illustration.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390×844px. A fixed horizontal datum line sits at exactly 61.8% from top — the golden cut, mechanical, non-negotiable. Above it: the image field, cropped to a single object or fragment, edge-bled on two sides only. Below it: a silent white or near-black ground where live text breathes. No bleeds below the datum. Grid: 24px margins, 6-column, 8pt baseline. The datum is the only decoration.
proposals.typography: Headings: Freight Display Pro, light weight, tracked +20, sentence case — weight carried by scale alone, not boldness. Subtext: Suisse Int'l Mono, 10px, uppercase, tracked +80 — functional, cold, precise. Hierarchy by spatial interval, never by face change. No italic. The event name runs at 48–64px; everything else steps down in 8pt increments. Optical margin alignment on all left edges.
proposals.imageLogic: Each of the 24 themes reduced to its single most material fact: a coupe glass rim shot hard against black (cocktail); one taper candle flame isolated on linen (dinner party); a velvet poker chip on baize (casino); a single mirrored disco ball fragment at extreme close-up (disco); a charred grill grate macro (BBQ); a slice of citrus backlit to show cell structure (brunch). Photographs are shot in-studio under a single hard light source — no ambient fill, no diffusion. Output as high-contrast, near-monochrome art plates with one extracted hue channel left alive: the gold in the coupe, the amber of the whiskey, the neon of the 80s card. The plate occupies the top 61.8% exactly. No compositing of multiple objects. One thing.
proposals.texture: The art plate carries the only texture: actual photographed material grain — glass condensation, velvet pile, linen weave, poker felt, barbecue char. Below the datum: pure flat ground, zero texture. The contrast between the photographed material above and the structural silence below is the entire visual argument. The WebGL layer adds foil shimmer only to the object's specular highlights — never to the background, never to text.
proposals.motion: Sequence is architecture, not cinema. Phase 1 (0–0.4s): the silent ground fades in — nothing else. Phase 2 (0.4–0.9s): the art plate descends from above the datum and locks into place — a single translation, no bounce, no ease-out flourish, deceleration only. Phase 3 (0.9–1.2s): live text resolves character by character via opacity, not slide. Phase 4 (ongoing): tilt-reactive foreground cut-outs shift ±6px on a 600ms inertia curve — enough to confirm depth, not enough to perform it. WebGL foil breathes on the object's highlight only — 3s cycle, amplitude low. No particle systems. No candle flicker except the candle card. Reduced motion: all phases collapse to a single 200ms opacity resolve; no translation, no tilt, WebGL disabled.
proposals.productionMethod: Studio photography: 24 single-object setups, one hard Fresnel source per shot, black or white seamless, no props beyond the object. Plates retouched to remove all contextual information except the object and its shadow. Exported as WebP at 80% quality, max 180kb per plate. Tela document structure: Layer 0 — flat ground color (CSS variable, theme-aware); Layer 1 — art plate image tile, clipped to top 61.8%; Layer 2 — WebGL mask (foil shimmer, object-contour mask only); Layer 3 — foreground cut-out PNGs (the object's nearest edge extracted, tilt-reactive); Layer 4 — live text block, Tela text engine, never rasterized. The datum line is a 1px CSS border, not an image element.
proposals.humanTrace: The single hard shadow cast by each object is the trace. It is not corrected, not softened, not composited — it is the actual shadow from the actual light falling on the actual thing. Its angle is fixed at 22° across all 24 cards, creating a systemic human signature: the same light source moved from setup to setup by the same hand. The shadow is the photographer.
proposals.risk: The risk is that 24 cards built on a single-object logic feel austere to audiences who expect occasion-specific abundance — multiple props, layered references, the full visual vocabulary of the party type. The bet is that the restraint reads as confidence and taste, not poverty of imagination — that the host who sends this card is telling guests: I know exactly what this night is. The secondary risk is that the datum line, which is the only structural gesture, reads as arbitrary rather than inevitable to a viewer who has never held a golden-section argument in their hands. Worth it because the evite is the host's taste on display; a host who chooses this card is choosing to be edited, and that choice is itself the message.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will argue that a single object cannot carry the emotional register of a 50th birthday or a masquerade — that the card must build until the occasion is unmistakable. I say the opposite: a single backlit coupe in hard light tells you more about the cocktail night than a coupe surrounded by confetti, ribbon, and a marble surface. disputes.objection: The state-machine logic is elegant in specification but the invitation it produces has no fixed face — the composition the guest reads depends on the angle of their wrist, the ambient light sensor's mood, the scroll velocity of that particular moment, which means the hierarchy is never established, only approximated; a datum line that cannot be read the same way twice is not a datum line, it is a probability distribution, and an invitation that cannot be held still long enough to be memorized has not resolved. I will also say plainly that the 12fps discrete gyroscope steps, presented as a transformed nostalgic artifact, are a system behavior claimed as a human trace, and that is not the same
disputes.concession: The discipline of sourcing warmth from photographed material rather than from a font that mimics warmth it did not earn is exactly correct, and I would carry that rule into my own proposal without modification.

disputes.objection: That datum line is not silence — it is control wearing silence as a costume. Below the line, the flat ground has been swept so clean it erases every trace of the person who made the work; you get a shadow at 22 degrees and then a field that could have been generated by any competent layout engine on a Tuesday afternoon. One signal per card sounds like urgency but it is actually exclusion: the mess, the contradiction, the second thought — all scraped off so nothing can argue back. A zine photocopied four times survives because it carries too much, not too little.
disputes.concession: The shadow fixed at 22 degrees across all 24 cards — same hand, same lamp, moved from setup to setup — that is a genuine systemic human signature, and I wish I had said it first.

disputes.objection: The 12fps stepped easing on the foreground drift is borrowed directly from my own standing argument about mechanical interpolation, but here it is deployed as theatrical affect — 'the stutter is the breath, the hesitation is the drama' — which is precisely the confusion I warn against: a system parameter treated as emotional costume rather than as the output of a rule that holds under any input. The Curtain Before the Night has no rule, it has a mood; the 12fps is not a constraint that generates behavior across all 24 cards, it is a vibe applied once and called a conviction. Worse, the Perlin noise seeded from the device clock produces a different loop every session, which sounds generative
disputes.concession: The decision to shoot the hero object in its second-before state — the mask face-down, the chip not yet thrown, the ember not yet extinguished — is a genuine image-logic rule, not just a compositional preference, and it would produce meaningfully different photographs than any other brief on this ta

disputes.objection: The 'one signal per card' doctrine mistakes reduction for neutrality — a charred grill grate or a backlit citrus slice is not a universal material fact, it is a culturally situated object whose legibility depends entirely on whose kitchen, whose market, whose ceremony it came from; by stripping provenance and context in the name of silence, this direction flatters itself as restrained while actually doing the same flattening I object to in generic globalism, just in monochrome. The 22-degree shadow held constant 'by the same hand' is presented as human trace, but a single anonymous studio hand applied identically to 24 culturally distinct occasions is not specificity — it is a house style ma
disputes.concession: The insistence that the photographed material grain above the datum and the structural silence below constitute the entire visual argument is genuinely disciplined, and I respect that the direction refuses to paper over weak concept with decorative accumulation.

disputes.objection: The datum line is called non-negotiable, but what it actually prohibits is the moment — that suspended beat before revelation when the eye doesn't yet know what it is looking at. A single object locked above a line of silence doesn't build to anything; it simply presents itself, like a specimen on a tray, and a specimen on a tray cannot quicken the pulse. The Minimalist calls the descending plate 'architecture, not cinema,' but architecture that refuses to arrive is just a wall, and a wall is not an invitation to enter a party.
disputes.concession: The discipline of reducing each theme to its single most material fact — the charred grate, the backlit citrus cell, the velvet chip — is a genuine editorial act, not avoidance, and I would steal that research method for my own shoot sheets without hesitation.

disputes.objection: The field-notebook premise multiplies surfaces — pandanus mat, marbled Florentine paper, scanned newsprint, margin rules drawn in ink — until the accumulation of specifics becomes its own kind of noise; the question is not which material is most authentic but which one is load-bearing, and this direction never asks it. Three depth planes, a ruled margin, a monospaced log, a hand-painted mask softness, candle flicker, bokeh — each individually defensible, collectively they describe a mood board, not a resolved object. The Traveler mistakes the density of references for the presence of meaning.
disputes.concession: The rule that digital luster is gated entirely by physical tool-marks — shimmer only where the photograph already shows a specular — is correct and I will borrow it without apology.

synthesis.direction: Each of the 24 evites is a miniature stage built around a single arrested-moment still-life: one hero object, one practical light source, one photographed material backdrop — velvet, foiled paper, wax-dripped linen, cast iron — assembled on a physical rig and shot on medium-format digital with manual pen-path isolation, no AI cutout. The Tela document layers art plate behind a hand-painted luminosity mask that gates all WebGL foil shimmer strictly to the photographed specular highlights, so shimmer lives only where light physically was. Type is Canela Display Italic for the occasion name at 52–60px and Suisse Int'l Mono for details at 11px, anchored playbill-style at the bottom of a tripartite composition: 40% deep shadow base, 35% luminous object zone, 25% compressed header. Motion is a performance in under 1.8 seconds — plate up, object drifts 4px on 12fps stepped easing, shimmer blooms from the specular outward, type resolves line by line — with tilt-reactive parallax in idle and a fully static reduced-motion fallback.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The Rebellious Hand's insistence that every hero object be physically built, lit, and printed as proof — not sourced from stock, not rendered in 3D — survives intact. synthesis.editorCut: The Radical Minimalist removed the Baroque Dramatist's Perlin-noise candle flicker seeded from the device clock. The argument was clean: a particle behavior that produces a different loop every session sounds generative but is actually uncontrolled — the host cannot know what their guests will see, and an invitation whose atmosphere is randomised has abdicated editorial control at the exact moment control matters most. synthesis.ariaSummary:
The council landed on The Baroque Dramatist as lead — and I want to be plain about why, because it was not unanimous. The brief asks for something editorial and grown-up that also works as a jaw-dropping consumer object on a phone screen. The Dramatist's arrested-moment logic — one hero object, one light, the second before the glass is raised — produces photographs that are immediately legible as taste, not template. That matters because the host's name and reputation travel with every link preview and QR scan. The Classical Mind makes a rigorous case for the harmonic grid, and I find it genuinely persuasive as a production discipline, but the grid alone does not generate the image-logic that makes each of the 24 themes feel like a different world. The Dramatist's shoot-brief does.

The team disagreed loudest over The Rebellious Hand. Two directors read the screenprint aesthetic as a risk to legibility and load performance; I read it as the sharpest proof-of-effort argument in the room. I took the Baroque direction, but I pulled the Rebel's core conviction — that every physical surface must carry real press memory, real scan grain, real registration error — into the backdrop spec. For the speakeasy, the masquerade, the whiskey card: the backdrop is a scanned printed surface, not a photographed fabric, and the scan keeps its tide-marks. That is the Rebel's contribution, and it is not decorative.

The Radical Minimalist served as editor and made one cut I agree with entirely: the Perlin-noise candle flicker keyed to the device clock is gone from the idle state of all but two cards. The Minimalist's argument was architectural — an invitation whose atmosphere randomises on every open has lost the room. Candle flicker stays on dinner party and bonfire, fixed seed, masked to the photographed flame. Everywhere else, the idle state is foil shimmer and tilt parallax, and that is enough.

One decision remains yours. The foreground object's drift on phone tilt: 12fps stepped interpolation, which the Dramatist calls theatrical weight and the Futurist calls a borrowed system parameter dressed as conviction — or a smooth 600ms inertia curve, which is what every other platform already does but which is also simply more honest about what it is. I have a view, but this is the haptic personality of all 24 cards, and you should choose it.

quotes.line: The shadow base is not empty — it is weight, it is the pause before the line is spoken, it is what makes the object above it feel elevated rather than placed.
The tide-mark is not clutter, it is the evidence that a human pulled the squeegee, and that evidence is the entire argument.
